summary: Auto-allocation failing: vendor payee name variation triggers manual review and split-payment hold
description:
Issue summary:
Accounts Payable auto-allocation is failing for a batch of supplier invoices where the payee name in the invoice (free-text) does not match the canonical vendor record. The payments pipeline flags these invoices for manual review and, for some, splits the payment across multiple ledger entities, causing a hold on the scheduled payout run.

Impact:
- 18 invoices (total $45,920 USD) stuck in 'manual review' state preventing the weekly payrun (next run scheduled 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC).
- Affected suppliers include two recurring vendors: Nimbus Data Services and Hightide Consulting.
- Finance ops cannot release payments until manual reconciliation is completed; this may cause late fees with one supplier.

Environment:
- Production AP pipeline (payments-engine v3.6.1)
- Reconciliation microservice (recon-svc v2.1.0)
- Vendor master reference: vendor_master-prod (region: us-west)

Observed behavior:
- Invoices with payee names like 'Nimbus Data, LLC' and 'Nimbus Data Services Inc.' did not match vendor_master entry 'Nimbus Data Services'. The auto-match routine returns status NOT_MATCHED and _split_allocation: true_ for some invoices where the system attempted to allocate across two subsidiary entities (US / EU) based on ambiguous tax id missing.
- Logs show payee_normalizer returning two candidate matches and the matching scorer falling below the threshold (score 0.62, threshold 0.75).
- The payments scheduler flagged these invoices and excluded them from the commit file for the ACH run.

Expected behavior:
- Minor variations in legal suffix (LLC/Inc./Ltd) and punctuation should be normalized and match the vendor_master entry when tax ID or bank account matches are present. If ambiguous, the system should surface a single tentative match instead of triggering split allocations.

Steps to reproduce (observed on prod ingestion flow):
1) Upload invoice PDF with payee header 'Nimbus Data, LLC' and tax id empty via AP UI.
2) Ingested by OCR/ingest pipeline (ingest-svc v1.8.0) which emits payee_name = 'Nimbus Data, LLC'.
3) Auto-match executed by payments-engine; normalizer emits candidates ["Nimbus Data Services","Nimbus Data"], scorer returns top score 0.62.
4) Matching logic treats score < 0.75 and missing tax id as ambiguous -> sets split_allocation=true and routes to manual-review queue.

Attachments / logs (snippets):
- payments-engine.log (2026-03-10T14:04:22Z): MATCH_ATTEMPT invoice=INV-2026-0034 payee_raw='Nimbus Data, LLC' candidates=['Nimbus Data Services','Nimbus Data'] scores=[0.62,0.58] result=NOT_MATCHED
- recon-svc.log (2026-03-10T14:04:25Z): ALLOCATION_DECISION invoice=INV-2026-0034 split_allocation=true reason='ambiguous_tax_id'
- scheduler.log (2026-03-11T01:50:00Z): PAYRUN_EXCLUDE invoice=INV-2026-0034 status='manual_review' payrun=2026-03-13

Relevant links:
- Slack thread: #finance-ops (thread t12345)
- Confluence: /display/FIN/Payee+Normalization+Runbook

Notes:
- This problem started spiking on 2026-03-08 after deploy of payments-engine v3.6.1 (PR #5462). We should consider whether the new fuzzy-matcher thresholds or the recent change to split allocation behavior (INT-329012) are related.
steps_to_reproduce: Upload invoice PDF with payee 'Nimbus Data, LLC' via AP UI
Confirm OCR sets payee_name = 'Nimbus Data, LLC'
Observe payments-engine matching run and candidate scores
See invoice routed to manual-review with split_allocation=true and excluded from next payrun

comments: 2026-03-10 15:12 - Priya Kapoor (Finance Ops): Flagged batch in #finance-ops — 18 invoices pending manual review. Requested engineering assist to avoid weekly payrun miss.

2026-03-10 16:30 - Mateo Ruiz (Platform Eng): Reproduced locally against prod snapshot. Fuzzy matcher top score frequently 0.58-0.66 for these payee variations. Investigating threshold change in v3.6.1 PR #5462.
2026-03-11 09:04 - Priya Kapoor (Finance Ops): One supplier (Hightide Consulting) emailed about possible late fee. Holding payments is high-impact. Prioritize please.

2026-03-11 11:20 - Mateo Ruiz (Platform Eng): Temporary workaround proposed: lower matching threshold from 0.75 to 0.65 for known-repeating vendors when bank account or tax id partially matches. Will run canary for today's manual review queue.

2026-03-12 08:45 - Alyssa Chen (Finance Ops Manager): Approved canary change for vendor whitelist. Asked engineering to prepare rollback plan and to add a more explicit audit flag in the UI so CS can triage faster.

2026-03-12 10:10 - Mateo Ruiz (Platform Eng): Deployed canary to 10% of payruns and ran reconciliation script to re-evaluate 18 invoices; 12 moved to AUTO_MATCH and included in staging payrun commit. Monitoring for false positives.
investigation_notes: Change introduced in payments-engine v3.6.1 tightened fuzzy-matcher threshold from 0.7 -> 0.75 (PR #5462).
Normalizer treats legal suffixes (LLC/Inc) differently now; normalization rule set v1.4 removed some aliasing entries for 'Nimbus' cluster.
Short-term fix: apply vendor-whitelist override to reduce threshold for repeated vendors with prior matching history.
Long-term: expand canonical alias table, add deterministic matching fallback using bank_account and tax_id precedence, and add clearer triage UI metadata (candidate scores visible to ops).
resolution: Temporary mitigation: Deployed threshold override for vendor-whitelist (applied to Nimbus & Hightide) and reprocessed the 18 invoices; 12 auto-matched and scheduled for inclusion in next payrun. Remaining 6 require manual tax-id confirmation. Follow-up action items created: 1) Reintroduce alias mappings for 'Nimbus' cluster (PR draft created), 2) Add bank-account-first deterministic matching path, 3) Add audit view for match-candidates in AP UI. Planned permanent fix timeline: deploy alias mapping and deterministic path by 2026-03-20.
